title: After the exam
lede: Results arrive faster than most people expect. What to look at, and in what order.

blocks.title: Performance is visible within minutes
blocks.text: Once students upload their answer files, the **assessment overview** in the portal gives you a first read on how the class did. You do not wait for a batch process or for OME to send you anything.

items.d: Distribution and overall performance. This is your sanity check that the exam behaved as intended.
Find questions where the whole class failed or where the distractors did not discriminate. These are your candidates for scoring adjustment and for retirement before next year.
This is what the category tags were for. A report can show category performance as a summary or broken out by exam taker, which is how you see whether a topic landed across the cohort.

blocks.title: Scoring adjustments are a deliberate act
blocks.text: If an item was defective, scoring can be adjusted after the fact — accepting a second correct answer, or dropping the item. Do this in consultation with OME, not unilaterally, because it changes the record for every student in the cohort.
Note the annual loop: the item analysis you run this year is what tells you which questions to remove when you duplicate this exam next year. See [Building an assessment](#building).
